//: Workload prototypes for the node sizing step (app/src-tauri/src/ai.rs).
//about: Seven shapes a node can be. The sizing step embeds the user's description with the
bundled all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model, embeds each prototype's `text` with the SAME model,
and picks the closest by cosine similarity.
Prototype vectors are deliberately NOT stored here. Embedding the texts at load time
guarantees the prototypes live in the same vector space as the description, whatever
model file is actually present -- a checked-in vector would silently become garbage
the day the model is replaced or requantised, and nothing would report it.
`keywords` drives the deterministic fallback used when the model cannot be loaded.
It is blunt on purpose: it is meant to be predictable and explainable, not clever.
Weights are relative within a prototype; a term unique to one shape earns more than
//quota: Splits follow the base 60/15/10/10/5 profile from include/desentry/common/config.h,
except where a workload's costs genuinely sit elsewhere: vector search pays for its
index (+15 to cache/index, taken from collections) and time series pays for a much
busier ledger (+10 to ledger, taken from collections).
//confidence_floor: Below this the wizard stops proposing and makes the user pick engines. It is a real threshold, not a display nicety.

prototypes.label: Relational
prototypes.text: Structured records in tables with fixed columns and clear relationships between them, queried with joins, filters and aggregates, where every row has the same shape and referential consistency matters.
texts: Customer orders, receipts, and inventory stored in normalised relational tables with foreign keys and referential integrity, queried with SQL joins.
Relational schema with primary keys, foreign key constraints, multi-table joins, and ACID transaction guarantees.

rationale.summary: Structured tabular records with fixed schemas, primary keys, foreign key constraints, and relational joins.

engine_rationales.sqlite: Full SQL relational engine with foreign key enforcement, B+Tree page indexing, and transactional ACID guarantees.
engine_rationales.kv: Secondary key-value fallback storage for raw blob cache and unindexed configuration records.

rationale.quota_rationale: Standard 60% database page cache allocation to optimize query plan execution and buffer B+Tree table pages.
trade_offs: Schema changes require explicit migration steps.
Foreign key cascades and secondary indexes increase write amplification.
Page-level concurrency is constrained compared to key-partitioned stores.

prototypes.label: Documents
prototypes.text: Self-contained JSON documents whose fields vary from one record to the next, fetched and written whole by key, with no fixed schema and no joins.
texts: User profile records and application documents stored as JSON blobs, retrieved directly by document ID without a schema.
Key-value document storage for variable JSON objects, fetched and updated by key without relational tables or joins.
Photos, videos, PDFs, and other uploaded files stored as binary blobs with metadata and fetched by asset ID.
A media library that stores image files and their filenames, captions, and metadata without searching by visual similarity.

rationale.summary: Flexible JSON document store with dynamic fields and key-based retrieval, without rigid schema constraints.

engine_rationales.kv: High-throughput key-value engine offering single-hop point lookups and low-overhead document persistence without schema enforcement.

rationale.quota_rationale: Standard 60% DB buffer with 15% transit store to smoothly absorb bursts of unstructured JSON document writes.
trade_offs: Filtered queries without secondary indexes require scanning document collections.

prototypes.label: Time series
prototypes.text: Measurements stamped with a time and a series name, arriving continuously from sensors or meters, read back as ranges and averages over hours or days, and eventually thrown away once they are old enough.
texts: Continuous sensor readings, telemetry, and IoT temperature data stamped with timestamps, sampled periodically and rolled up.
Time-series monitoring metrics and device telemetry arriving continuously, downsampled and queried across time windows.

rationale.summary: High-frequency timestamped telemetry and metric series, optimized for streaming writes and time-window rollups.

engine_rationales.ts_rollup: Tiered time-series engine with automatic downsampling (raw -> 1m -> 1h), compact delta encoding, and scheduled retention pruning.
engine_rationales.kv: Fast lookup for latest measurement state and series registration metadata.

rationale.quota_rationale: Ledger increased to 20% (+10%) to provide a deep append-log buffer for uninterrupted streaming ingestion.
trade_offs: Expired records are permanently pruned based on retention policy.
Random past-timestamp writes require re-sorting rollup buckets.

prototypes.label: Vectors and similarity
prototypes.text: Embeddings of text or images stored as numeric vectors and searched by similarity, so that asking for something returns the nearest matches by meaning rather than by exact value.
texts: High-dimensional numeric vector embeddings searched with cosine similarity for semantic recommendations and nearest neighbor retrieval.
Vector embeddings index for neural search, RAG retrieval pipelines, and cosine similarity matching over embedding vectors.
Images converted into embeddings and searched for visually similar pictures or nearest matching images.
Reverse image search using visual feature vectors to find photos with similar content.

rationale.summary: High-dimensional vector embeddings indexed for semantic retrieval and approximate nearest-neighbor similarity.

engine_rationales.vector_hnsw_lite: Hierarchical Navigable Small World graph index for sub-millisecond approximate nearest neighbor search over dense embeddings.
engine_rationales.kv: Stores associated text chunks, document payloads, and filter attributes linked to vector IDs.

rationale.quota_rationale: Cache/Index increased to 25% (+15%) to maintain the HNSW graph and vector index in memory for low-latency queries.
trade_offs: Higher memory consumption to keep the vector graph resident in RAM.
Building HNSW index edges incurs CPU overhead on batch vector ingestion.

prototypes.label: Graph
prototypes.text: Entities connected to other entities, where the connections are the point: parents and children, who follows whom, what depends on what, traversed outward from a starting node.
texts: Org chart of employees and managers, dependency graphs, and social networks traversed along relationships and edges between nodes.
Graph traversal across connected entities, finding paths between nodes, hierarchical trees, and network connections.

rationale.summary: Interconnected entities and directional relationships optimized for multi-hop graph traversals and hierarchy queries.

engine_rationales.graph_adj: Adjacency-list graph engine supporting fast pointer-chasing and deep recursive relationship traversals.
engine_rationales.kv: Stores vertex and edge property maps and metadata payloads.

rationale.quota_rationale: Standard 60% database page buffer to keep high-degree adjacency lists cached in memory.
trade_offs: Traversals on dense nodes can consume significant memory without depth limits.
Graph-wide pattern matching is more memory-intensive than flat table scans.

prototypes.label: Semi-structured
prototypes.text: Records that mostly share a shape but not entirely: logs, events, imported files and scraped data, where some fields are always present, others appear sometimes, and the whole lot has to be scanned and summarised.
texts: Clickstream analytics, server logs, and scraped events with mixed schemas, scanned and aggregated with columnar OLAP queries.
Batch import of CSV data and log records with variable fields, aggregated and summarised across millions of rows.

rationale.summary: Analytical event logs and tabular exports with variable schemas, optimized for columnar OLAP aggregations.

engine_rationales.duckdb: Vectorized analytical engine executing parallel scans and aggregations across millions of rows.
engine_rationales.columnar_lite: Lightweight built-in columnar format with dictionary compression for efficient range queries.
engine_rationales.kv: Ingestion buffer for raw events prior to columnar compaction.

rationale.quota_rationale: Standard 60% database buffer configured with wide block caching for sequential scan throughput.
trade_offs: Single-record write latency is higher than key-value stores due to columnar block construction.
OLAP memory consumption spikes during wide grouped aggregations.

prototypes.label: Objects over relational
prototypes.text: Objects with classes, inheritance and typed attributes, persisted into relational tables and read back as objects, so that the code works with instances while the storage stays queryable.
texts: Class hierarchy and polymorphic domain models persisted into relational tables via an ORM like SQLAlchemy or Hibernate.
Object-relational mapping (ORM) with inheritance trees, class entities, and object instance persistence.

rationale.summary: Object-oriented class hierarchies and domain models persisted transparently into relational tables and relationship graphs.

engine_rationales.graph_adj: Tracks class inheritance trees and polymorphic relationship pointers.
engine_rationales.sqlite: Stores flattened entity attributes and property columns in relational tables.
engine_rationales.kv: Fast object identity cache for active instances.

rationale.quota_rationale: Standard 60% database buffer allocated between tabular property tables and inheritance hierarchy graphs.
trade_offs: Object-relational mapping impedance incurs minor translation overhead.
Deep polymorphic queries may require multiple table joins or graph hops.
